paper.title: MetaClaw: Just Talk -- An Agent That Meta-Learns and Evolves in the Wild
paper.central_claim: MetaClaw: continual meta-learning that jointly maintains a base LLM policy and an evolving skill library; gradient-free skill evolution from failures takes effect immediately, while opportunistic LoRA RL (during user-idle windows) with skill-generation versioning separates support and query data; improves accuracy on MetaClaw-Bench (Kimi-K2.5 21.4%->40.6%) and robustness on AutoResearchClaw.

rationale: 技能库快速适应+LoRA慢适应，自建基准上有方向性收益；版本隔离、互促、OMLS均无消融，评测流即学习流，无方差，成本未量化。

expectations.reason: Skill evolution and RL use disjoint streams by design (support vs query); the shared interface is the version-stamped data, not the same rollouts.
Typed roles are argued (skills = declarative format rules, RL = execution reliability, Case 2) and task-type breakdown is consistent, but there is no weights-only arm to isolate each lever.
RL is run on trajectories collected under the evolving skill context; skills come from failures.
Avoidance of 'sequenced, not coupled' rests only on version stamps; mutual reinforcement is asserted (E027) without a test.
Reward is a learned PRM and only non-failure trajectories reach the buffer; how failure and PRM scores are defined/calibrated is not given.
Adaptation stream and reported stream are the same 30/14-day stream with no declared split.
Every sample carries its skill-generation index; stale samples are flushed.
No context-only/weights-only/coupled arms for both models; Full exists once for one model with no seeds or matched budget.
Skills are synthesized from failures only; no contrast with successes.
Add-only union; no consolidation, forgetting or conflict handling.
New skills take effect immediately with no execution/marginal-gain gate.
Skills-on vs skills-off with identical prompts and tools is the direct toggle for the skill arm.
Benchmark feedback states the hidden rules; no overlap/contamination or held-out stream analysis.
The stated gap (raw-trajectory memory is verbose) is never tested against a raw-trajectory/Reflexion-type memory baseline.
AutoResearchClaw is a second domain but skills-only, one topic, one A/B.
No variant mixing support and query data (versioning off).
Stale-reward harm is described but never measured.
No seeds, CI or repeated runs; Full is one 5-day run.
Automated checkers are objective but the benchmark and rules are the authors' and the feedback states the rule.
Sec.3.3 (accumulate across generations), Sec.3.4 (flush <= g) and Algorithm 1 (failures excluded) disagree about buffer content.

claims.text: Skill-driven fast adaptation alone improves accuracy by up to 32% relative.
claims.setting: MetaClaw-Bench Part I (346 Q, 30 days) and II (588 Q, 14 days); GPT-5.2, Kimi-K2.5
claims.baseline_control: Same model and prompts without skills
claims.selection_vs_test: Online stream; skills learned from earlier days applied to later days; no separate held-out stream
claims.result_denominator: Accuracy: GPT 41.1->44.0, 44.9->49.1; Kimi 21.4->28.3, 21.1->26.9; completion unchanged on Part I
claims.allowed_conclusion: On this authored simulation, skills-on beats skills-off by roughly 3-7 accuracy points in single runs; Part I completion is not improved.

claims.text: The full pipeline (skills + opportunistic RL) lifts Kimi-K2.5 from 21.4% to 40.6% and completion 8.25x, nearly matching GPT-5.2.
claims.selection_vs_test: RL trained on the same stream it is evaluated on (continual)
claims.result_denominator: Part I acc 40.6, compl 16.5; Part II acc 39.6, compl 51.9; multi-choice declines
claims.allowed_conclusion: Full > skills-only > baseline for one model/run on this stream; RL's own contribution vs in-stream fine-tuning generally, and skills/weights mutual reinforcement, are not isolated.

claims.text: Skill-generation versioning prevents stale-reward contamination and is essential; OMLS removes downtime.
claims.allowed_conclusion: Untested design claims; text on buffer contents is inconsistent.

claims.text: Skill injection alone improves AutoResearchClaw composite robustness by 18.3% (cross-domain generalization).
claims.selection_vs_test: later runs reuse skills from earlier runs of the same topic
claims.allowed_conclusion: One same-topic A/B with an author-defined process metric; supports plausibility only.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On the authors' simulated 30/14-day CLI stream, failure-distilled prompt skills accumulated over the stream raise later-day accuracy by about 3-7 points over a no-skill run (single runs); a 5-day LoRA RL run on one model adds further gains whose attribution is not isolated.
assessment.unresolved: Versioning/OMLS/retrieval necessity; weights-only control; real-user transfer; buffer semantics; cost; variance; nearest neighbours uncompared.

G.reason: Concrete gap (static skill libs, stale RL rewards after skill change) with named related work categories, but the absolute 'no existing system' claim is untested and closest co-evolution neighbours are not compared.

M.reason: Two-timescale design is coherent and the support/query rationale is clear, but the 'meta-learning' framing is loose (evolver is not optimized), and RL-buffer rules conflict (accumulate across generations vs flush vs failures excluded).

X.reason: Algorithm, versioning rule, OMLS signals and evolver prompt are given, but k/embedder/failure threshold/evolver model/PRM are unspecified, the library is add-only without gate or rollback, and buffer semantics are inconsistent.

E.measurement.reason: Deterministic checkers and accuracy/completion metrics are usable, but the benchmark is self-authored with rule-revealing feedback, RL reward is a learned PRM, and the AutoResearchClaw composite is an author-defined process metric.

E.causality.reason: Skills-on/off is a valid toggle for the skill arm, but there is no weights-only arm, no versioning/OMLS/retrieval ablation, no cheaper-memory baseline, and Full is one run on one model.

E.holdout.reason: Learning and reporting stream coincide with no declared split; rules are revealed in feedback; the second domain reuses a single topic across runs.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes (346/588 questions) and negative cells are reported, but no variance, seeds or tests; single Full run.

E.cost.reason: Qualitative cost statements only (zero downtime, no local GPU, 5-day run); no GPU hours, API cost, evolver/PRM calls or prompt-token overhead.
